title: Gate Rust CI on JavaScript CI, add a parity manifest and agent push-gate rules, and align CI with the pipeline templates
body:
## Problem

relative-meta-logic has a JavaScript implementation (`js/src`, about 9k lines in `rml-links.mjs` alone) and a Rust one (`rust/src/lib.rs`, 14k lines). Parity is checked, but the CI/CD does not follow the standard from link-assistant/router#759 or the shared pipeline templates. Rust jobs can start without a green JavaScript stage, there is no parity manifest, there are no agent rules for bulk drafting with a single push, and the usual release, link, security and workflow-lint pipelines are missing. Draft PR #184 (+400,307 lines, 100 commits, open since 2026-09-20) shows the cost: its branch `issue-183-7fedfddffe9c` has 22 failed and 1 cancelled `issue-183-acceptance` runs and 0 green, 5 failed `formal-corpus`, 4 failed `tests`, 7 failed `cache-portability`, 3 failed `orientation-proofs`, and 2 cancelled `tests` runs.

## Findings

1. No gate between the JavaScript and Rust stages. `.github/workflows/tests.yml` has jobs `js` and `rust` side by side with no `needs:`. `parity.yml` builds Rust (`cargo build --bin rml`) in the same job as the JavaScript steps. `docker.yml` builds both. A failing JavaScript job does not stop Rust from starting.
2. Path filters can skip checks. `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml` and `docker.yml` run only for listed paths (for example `parity.yml` does not list `scripts/**` other than two files, `lib/**`, or `examples/**`), while `tests.yml` has no filter. Different workflows therefore run on different subsets of changes, and no single required check covers all of them.
3. No branch protection on `main` (`gh api repos/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected"), so nothing makes any stage required.
4. The `parity` workflow (green 15/15 on #184, 26/26 on the branch) verifies only one thing: `scripts/check-corpus-parity.mjs` runs `test-corpus/` through the JS CLI and the Rust `rml` binary and compares stdout and exit status. It is a useful output check, but there is no parity manifest (no file listing each feature with its JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation and evidence), so features that are not in the corpus (LSP, CST, Lean/Rocq export, the `rml-check` and `rml-meta` binaries, the large linked-semantics surface in #184) have no parity check. Because the workflow is green by construction on the corpus, its green status does not tell whether the 13 other checks in #184 pass.
5. Rust is hand-written in parallel with JavaScript, not generated through meta-language. `rust/Cargo.toml` depends on the `meta-language` crate (0.49.0) and `js/package.json` on the npm package (^0.46.0), and the two versions differ. There is no translation step and no regenerate-and-diff check. `rust/src/lib.rs` is 14,205 lines and `js/src/rml-links.mjs` is 9,060 lines kept in sync by hand.
6. `concurrency` is missing in `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml`, `docker.yml`, `lint-english.yml`. Only `tests.yml` (cancel on non-main) and `api-docs.yml` have it. With push-per-fix this produces overlapping runs; the branch of #184 has 26 runs of each of these workflows.
7. Rust build load is not configured: `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.*]` section (no `debug = "line-tables-only"` or `debug = 0`, no `incremental = false` for CI), there is no `.cargo/config.toml`, no `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` or `-j` limit in any workflow, and no artifact pruning. `tests.yml` caches with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, but `parity.yml` and `docker.yml` build Rust without a cache. `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `rust-version`.
8. No agent instructions. The repository has no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so there are no rules for bulk drafting sub-agents and a single push gate. #184 reached 100 commits with many red runs.
9. Differences from the templates (rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template):
   - Missing workflows: `release.yml` (version, changelog fragments, publish), `links.yml` (lychee link check, no `lychee.toml`), `security.yml`, `workflows.yml` (workflow lint). There is no `changelog.d/` or `CHANGELOG.md`, and no `dependabot.yml` or `renovate` config.
   - Action pinning is inconsistent: `tests.yml` uses `actions/checkout@v6`, but `parity.yml` and `bootstrap.yml` use `@v4` and `setup-node@v4`; none are pinned to a commit SHA.
   - Docker workflows (`docker.yml`) and `api-docs.yml` are the only publish-like flows; the crate (0.19.0) and npm package are never released by CI. This is partly covered by #185.
   - No false-positive/negative guards for CI (for example a check that every workflow's required job still exists).
10. Stale pull request: #184 is the only open PR (draft, open since 2026-09-20, last updated 2026-10-09), a single +400k line change too large to review that has never had a full green run. `main` itself is green (last 30 runs succeeded) but its last run was 2026-07-11.

## Requirements

1. Make Rust CI start only after JavaScript CI passes for the same commit: in `tests.yml` add `needs:` for every JavaScript job (lint, tests, parity, bootstrap, translation check) to the Rust jobs, or use `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`. Move the `cargo build` out of `parity.yml`'s first stage or make it depend on the JavaScript job. A cancelled, skipped or failed JavaScript run must not start Rust.
2. Remove path filters from the gate jobs (or add an always-run summary job that is skipped-safe) so a Rust-only change still runs the JavaScript, parity and bootstrap checks.
3. Enable branch protection on `main` requiring the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and parity.
4. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`) listing each feature with its JavaScript and Rust implementation and test evidence, and a checker script run in both the JS and Rust stages that fails when a feature is missing on one side. Cover the CLI, `rml-check`, `rml-meta`, LSP/CST, Lean/Rocq export and the linked-semantics surface of #184, not only `test-corpus/`.
5. Add a translation step from the JavaScript source to Rust through meta-language with a regenerate-and-diff check, or document in `docs/` exactly which parts cannot be translated yet, keep them listed in the manifest, and report each gap to link-foundation/meta-language with a minimal example. Align the `meta-language` versions in `rust/Cargo.toml` and `js/package.json`.
6. Add `concurrency` groups to `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml`, `docker.yml` and `lint-english.yml` (cancel in progress for pull requests, not for the Rust stage after the gate, not for `main`).
7. Add a Rust build profile and CI settings: `debug = "line-tables-only"` (or `0`) and `incremental = false` for CI, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `-j` limited, `Swatinem/rust-cache` in every workflow that builds Rust, a shared bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for local use, and a documented prune step. Set `rust-version`.
8. Add `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` describing: drafting sub-agents never push; exactly one CI/CD sub-agent pushes, once per batch of fixes for all failures of the last run; no push while a run for the same commits is in progress; JavaScript checks locally, Rust builds locally only for Rust-only changes.
9. Bring the CI in line with the templates: add `release.yml` (changelog fragments in `changelog.d/`, version bump, crates.io and npm publish; coordinate with #185), `links.yml` with `lychee.toml`, `security.yml`, `workflows.yml` (workflow lint), a dependency update config; pin actions to one major version consistently (`checkout@v6`, `setup-node@v6`) or to SHAs. Add a CI check that fails if any workflow can start Rust jobs without the JavaScript gate.
10. Split or land #184 in reviewable pieces, and make `issue-183-acceptance`, `formal-corpus` and `tests` pass or remove them from the required set with a recorded reason. Record before/after numbers (pushes per PR, runs per PR green/failed/cancelled) in `docs/case-studies/`.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (the standard and this audit)
- link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 (crate/npm publishing and release workflow; partly covers requirement 9 release flow)
- link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#183 and PR #184 (the red acceptance checks)
- link-foundation/meta-language (translation gaps)

---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
